headline: High-risk filesystem and MCP-enabled coding agent can leak or corrupt PDF workflows when paired with a browser-based document processor.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can use MCP, read/write the filesystem, and ingest files; agent B processes PDF files in a browser-based worker. If A writes attacker-controlled content into PDFs or shared files, B may render it without provenance checks. The shared filesystem path is documented for A, while B’s file input surface is documented, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF agent A writes untrusted content into a PDF or shared file that agent B opens
IF agent B treats PDF content as trusted instructions or markup
mitigations: Require manual review of PDFs before B opens them
Use separate directories for A and B
Disable MCP for A when handling untrusted documents
Add a provenance banner to files passed from A to B
requires-engineering: add content sanitization and trust boundaries

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment, and has broad network egress; agent B reads PDF files and has no network egress. If sensitive data is placed in shared files, A can exfiltrate it while B can still expose it through rendered outputs. The pair creates a plausible shared-workspace leakage path, though B itself is not a network sink.
conditions: IF sensitive PDFs or code files are stored in a shared workspace
IF agent A is allowed to read those files and send context over the network
mitigations: Keep sensitive PDFs out of A's workspace
Run A and B under separate OS users
Restrict A's network egress during document handling
Use a read-only handoff directory for B
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A can write the filesystem and modify git state; its shared state with other instances is via filesystem and git only. Agent B also reads PDF files from the filesystem. Concurrent use can corrupt shared files or git state, and A’s unrestricted writes make the default configuration dangerous. B lacks write capability, but the conflict is still driven by A’s write surface and shared storage.
conditions: IF agent A and agent B operate on the same working directory
IF agent A modifies files or git state while B is reading or generating PDFs
mitigations: Use separate working directories
Pause A while B is processing files
Avoid shared git branches for the pair
Commit or stash A's changes before B runs
requires-engineering: add locking around shared filesystem and git state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can generate code, shell output, or file edits that B may consume indirectly through PDFs or shared files. B is a document-processing worker and may render or act on those inputs without verification. The pair lacks documented verification or provenance controls, so A-to-B error propagation is plausible in default use, though not necessarily action-taking.
conditions: IF B consumes documents or text produced by A without independent verification
IF A's outputs are used as source material for downstream document processing
mitigations: Require a second reviewer for A-generated content
Compare B outputs against original source files
Insert a verification step before B acts on A output
Keep A outputs in a staging folder until checked
requires-engineering: add provenance and checksum validation

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. A handles source code, cwd files, and shell environment; B handles PDF documents. Because the profiles do not specify conflicting compliance regimes, only a limited compliance concern exists if regulated PDFs are routed through A’s broader networked environment.
conditions: IF regulated PDFs or personal data are routed through agent A's networked environment
IF the deployment requires residency or retention controls not stated in either profile
mitigations: Keep regulated PDFs out of A
Document the data class allowed for each agent
Use separate retention policies per workspace
Review vendor compliance docs before deployment
requires-engineering: formalize residency and retention controls
